chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Ali Al-Būfaki, who said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, and he was in the service of Abī Ja’far the Second (peace be upon him), from ‘Ali, from Safwān ibn Mihrān Al-Jammāl, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), in a long ḥadīth:

I asked him: 'Whoever visits him and then departs, when should he return to him? And how often should he be visited? And what is the maximum time people are allowed to stay away from him?' He replied: 'It is not permissible to stay away for more than a month. As for those who live far away, [they should visit] once every three years. Whoever passes three years without visiting him, has been ungrateful to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and has severed his honor, except for one with a valid excuse.'

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي: Abū Ja'far al-Thānī (Imam al-Jawād, peace be upon him)
key_terms.بَعِيدُ الدَّارِ: One who lives far away (distant traveler)
key_terms.عَقَّ: To be ungrateful / to neglect duty severely

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum required frequency for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) for locals and distant travelers?
ai.summary: This ḥadīth from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the jurisprudential boundaries for Ziyārah frequency, distinguishing between local residents (monthly) and distant travelers (every three years). It elevates the act of visitation beyond mere ritual to a covenant of loyalty, where prolonged neglect without valid excuse is equated with 'breaking the honor' (qata'a hurmatahu) of the Prophet, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining spiritual ties (silat al-rahim) with the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 13. My father narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, and from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Ali Al-Būfaki, from Yaḥyā – who was the servant of Abī Ja’far the Second (Imam Jawād (a.s.)), from ‘Ali, from Safwān ibn Mihrān Al-Jammāl, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) – as part of a longer Ḥadīth, “After one returns from the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.), how soon should he return to his Ziyārah? And how often should one go to his Ziyārah? And what is the longest time one is allowed to stay away from his Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied: It is not permissible to stay away from his Ziyārah longer than a month (for those who live close to his grave). However, for those who live far from him, it (the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)) should be (performed at least) once every three years. If three years pass and they do not go to his Ziyārah, they are (considered) ungrateful to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and they have dishonoured him, except those who have a (valid) excuse.
